result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (6 tests, 3 files), and I verified the real path end to end: with `.env` as shipped (`QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync`, `MAIL_MAILER=log`) a registration prints the message to the server output and still redirects `303 → /dashboard`, while with `QUEUE_CONNECTION=memory`/`MAIL_MAILER=memory` the request leaves exactly one job waiting and zero mail sent, and running that job delivers exactly one message.

I brought up the queue and mailer the way this project structures such things — `bunx guren add queue` / `bunx guren add mail` scaffolding, then rewritten for real use: `app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts` builds the queue manager from `QUEUE_CONNECTION` (`sync`, `memory`, or `redis` — the Redis client is dynamically imported only when selected) and registers the job class at boot, and `app/Providers/MailProvider.ts` builds the mail manager from `MAIL_MAILER` (`log`, `memory`, `resend`) with the default sender from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`, publishing it via `setMailManager` so workers can reach it; both are wired into `src/app.ts` after the framework's `QueueServiceProvider`/`MailServiceProvider`. The message itself is `app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts` (subject `Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!` via a new `appName()` helper in `config/app.ts`, plain-text greeting by name), sent by `app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts`, which `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts` dispatches with `{ name, email }` only after the user is created and signed in — so a refused registration (validation error or taken email) returns before any dispatch and queues nothing. `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` covers all four cases against a holding queue and a recording transport, and the README documents the new flow and directories.
